title: Strict powers of degree-zero regular parameters in an adic filtration
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $M$ a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ an ideal. For $p\geq0$ put $E_p=I^pM/I^{p+1}M$, with scalar multiplication induced from $M$. Fix $s\geq0$ and $y_1,\ldots,y_s\in\mathfrak m$, and put $J=(y_1,\ldots,y_s)$. Assume that for every $p\geq0$ and $1\leq i\leq s$, multiplication by $y_i$ is injective on $E_p/(y_1,\ldots,y_{i-1})E_p$; this is the injectivity condition in [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], allowing $E_p=0$. Then for every $p,q\geq0$ one has the equality of submodules of $M$
$$I^pM\cap J^qM=J^q I^pM.$$
The empty parameter list, $I=0$, and $M=0$ are allowed.

source.place: Agent-written filtered-module synthesis; supporting Tags 0F1T (lemma-regular-sequence-short-exact-sequence), 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular, module version), and 00IP (lemma-intersect-powers-ideal-module-zero). None of these tags alone states this strictness theorem.

proof.text: Put $Q_a=M/I^aM$ for $a\geq0$. The list $y_1,\ldots,y_s$ satisfies the injectivity condition on every $Q_a$, by induction on $a$. The base is $Q_0=0$, on which every scalar is injective. For the induction step use the canonical short exact row $0\to E_{a-1}\to Q_a\to Q_{a-1}\to0$ for $a\geq1$. Part (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-short-exact-sequence] applies: its left-term injectivity is the hypothesis on $E_{a-1}$, and its right-term injectivity is the induction hypothesis. Its middle-term assertion gives the required condition on $Q_a$, even when a term is zero.

Fix $p,q\geq0$ and set $N=I^pM$, $Q=M/N$. For any $r\geq q$ and $z\in N\cap J^rM$, expand $z=\sum_{|\alpha|=r}y^\alpha m_\alpha$ with $m_\alpha\in M$; the monomials generate $J^r$ by expanding products of the generators of $J$. The image of this sum in $Q$ is zero. Apply [lem-trf-weak-regular-module-homogeneous-coefficients] to $Q$ with the injectivity proved in step 1: zero belongs to $J^{r+1}Q$, so every $\bar m_\alpha$ lies in $JQ$. Hence choose $a_{\alpha i}\in M$ and $n_\alpha\in N$ with $m_\alpha=n_\alpha+\sum_i y_i a_{\alpha i}$. Substitution gives $z=b+w$, where $b=\sum y^\alpha n_\alpha\in J^rN$ and $w=\sum_{\alpha,i}y^\alpha y_i a_{\alpha i}\in J^{r+1}M$. Since $z,b\in N$, also $w\in N$. Thus $N\cap J^rM\subseteq J^rN+(N\cap J^{r+1}M)$.

For $x\in N\cap J^qM$ prove by induction on $r\geq q$ that $x=b_r+z_r$ with $b_r\in J^qN$ and $z_r\in N\cap J^rM$. Start with $b_q=0$, $z_q=x$. Step 2 writes $z_r=c_r+z_{r+1}$ with $c_r\in J^rN\subseteq J^qN$ and $z_{r+1}\in N\cap J^{r+1}M$; take $b_{r+1}=b_r+c_r$. Consequently $x\in J^qN+J^rM$ for every $r\geq q$.

Let $P=M/J^qN$. It is finite: the images of a finite generating list of $M$ generate $P$. Step 3 puts the class of $x$ in $J^rP$ for every $r\geq q$; for $r<q$ use $J^qP\subseteq J^rP$. Since $R$ is Noetherian and local and $J\subseteq\mathfrak m=\operatorname{Jac}(R)$, [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] gives $\bigcap_{r\geq0}J^rP=0$. The class of $x$ is therefore zero, so $x\in J^qN$. Conversely, every summand $a n$ with $a\in J^q$ and $n\in N$ lies in both $N$ and $J^qM$, proving the reverse inclusion and the claimed equality. This also covers $p=0$, $q=0$, $I=0$, $M=0$ and the empty list ($J=0$).

Expose VIII, Theorems 3.1.27 and 3.2.20, and Remark 3.2.21, pp.102,106; construction in 3.2.19 over k=Q. Supporting source: Expose VIII, Theorem 2.3.10, normalized restriction in 2.3.9 and Remark 2.3.12(i), equivariance in Corollary 2.3.17, printed pp.93--95; application in 3.2.19, p.106. Refinement in this split: Expose VIII, Theorem 2.3.10 restricted to finite-type Q-schemes, with tower conventions 2.1.4, 2.3.1, 2.3.4 and Remark 2.3.5(i), printed pp.87,91--93. This is ordinary resolution, not the normalized toric conclusion; no Stacks tag states this characteristic-zero resolution theorem. Lower input: embedded characteristic-zero resolution and invariant synchronization discussed in ILO VIII 2.3.11 and 2.3.13; the intrinsic gluing argument is supplied in this item. Lower input: Expose VIII 2.3.11 and 2.3.13, pp.93--94: local invariant input underlying the cited strong embedded algorithm; BMT sections 6.1--6.3, especially local embedding independence and the correction of synchronization for arbitrary smooth morphisms. Lower input: Smooth-stable Hilbert--Samuel head and component-dimension correction. Refinement here: Component-dimension rigidity at a Hilbert--Samuel near point of a blowup. Supporting refinement: Normal-flat normal cone and linear vertex at a Hilbert--Samuel near point. Lower input here: Theorem 2.10(2), printed pp.32--33, and the characteristic-independent additive-subgroup argument in the proof of Theorem 2.14, printed p.36, before its linearity argument: Hironaka [H4], Certain numerical characters of singularities, Theorem IV, and [H5], Additive groups associated with points of a projective space, Theorem 2. The normal-cone quotient used there is Theorem 2.2(2)(ii), printed p.28. Refinement in Q87: Numerical near-point input: normal-cone equations have generators in the projective-point order algebra. Q103 refinement: section 2, p.153, normal-flat tangent/normal-cone comparison, and the paragraph after Example (4.2), p.157; the cited underlying result is Resolution of singularities (1964), Chapter II, Theorem 2; numerical input: the Hilbert function of a normally flat local ring is the convolution of the normal-cone fibre Hilbert function with the Hilbert function of its regular centre. Q28 refinement: algebraic strictness of powers of lifted centre parameters on the I-adic module filtration, used before taking finite-length factors.
